text:
Mike R: Quick follow-up from last week's control-plane split RFC. We didn't fully decide on the customer-agent <-> control-plane handshake and how that impacts peering/egress cost. putting the options + questions here so we can converge.

Darya P: Short version — we need an auth flow that supports short-lived creds + silent rotation. mTLS is nice but key distribution is the pain point for private deploys. KMS-backed signing + challenge-response looks clean.

Ben L: Agree on rotation. Also flag — if we go with per-customer NAT/peering we'll hit substantial NAT gateway egress costs in AWS. EIPs are cheaper for steady-state, but we lose elasticity.

Eunice: Another axis: operator simplicity vs tenant isolation. Options we discussed: sidecar agent (runs in customer VPC), regional relay (shared srv in our VPC with VPC Endpoint/PrivateLink), or per-tenant ENI/NAT. Each has different billing + failure modes.

Claire (sre): From SRE POV: tracing & incidentability are easier with a regional relay — single control plane egress point we can instrument. But blast radius is larger if relay fails. We need automatic fallback to public path.

Mike R: Listing the concrete tradeoffs so folks can vote: 
A) Sidecar agent with outbound tunnel to CP (no peering) — Pros: best isolation, low cross-account network cost; Cons: more per-tenant infra + rollout complexity.
B) Regional relay with PrivateLink endpoints — Pros: simple ops, central tracing, easier canary deployments; Cons: inter-region cost + possible throttling, requires us to absorb some egress.
C) Per-tenant peering + NAT/EIP — Pros: predictable routing, low latency; Cons: costly NAT, scaling peering is admin-heavy.

Ben L: +1 on enumerating. Quick note: option B can be hybrid — relay for control messages, direct data plane to dedicated GPUs for heavy inference to avoid double egress.

Darya P: Security proposal for the handshake (sketch):
```json
{
  "version": "1",
  "client_id": "tenant-123",
  "nonce": "base64",
  "signed": "kms-sig",
  "expires": "2025-07-01T12:00:00Z"
}
```
Server verifies signature or validates short-lived token issued by customer's KMS link. This avoids long-lived credentials in agents.

Eunice: Ops questions: rotation window? 1h or 24h? Shorter gives better security but more flapping when clocks drift. Also need to handle offline agents that cannot reach CP for rotation (air-gapped option).

Claire (sre): For rotation: default 1h with jitter + grace window 10m. Offline/air-gapped: allow manual heartbeats + offline certs with longer TTL and audited renew path. Documented in the private deployment runbook.

Mike R: Implementation sketch for graceful fallback (pseudocode):
```bash
# agent start
if can_connect(control_plane_private_endpoint):
  use_private_path()
else:
  fallback_public_api()
  start_backoff_reconnect()
fi
```
We need health-check semantics so control-plane knows an agent is running behind a NAT vs unreachable.

Darya P: Also add metrics labels: path=private|public, auth_method=kms|mtls, last_renew_ts. That lets Optimize and Console slice cost by routing policy.

Ben L: Another operational thought — if we keep control messages small (control plane state, rollouts) and route heavy payloads (model tokens) directly to dedicated model endpoints, we minimize egress on our side. Worth architecting the protocol to pass pointer+auth for heavy dataplane.

Eunice: I like pointer approach. That also means we need a tight model ACL system so dataplane endpoints accept requests pinned to tenant tokens.

Claire (sre): From incident playbook POV we should have: (1) detect relay saturation (QPS+latency), (2) auto-failover to alternate region, (3) telemetry export (request id chain). Will need tracing headers preserved across fallback.

infra-bot: Deployment scheduled: cp-handshake-proto/v1 -> canary on staging at 2025-06-18T09:00Z :rocket:

Mike R: Ask: can infra + security + SRE ack design A/B/C + handshake draft by EOD Friday? If yes we'll pick a primary path (prob hybrid B+pointer) and start a spike to prototype token exchange + private endpoint patterns.

Darya P: ACK from security. I'll write a short threat model for each option and post by Thursday.

Ben L: ACK from infra — will run cost projection for per-region relay vs NAT for our top 50 tenants.

Claire (sre): ACK. I'll add tracing & runbook checklist.

Mike R: Thanks all. I'll update the RFC with the handshake sketch and the fallback semantics. If anyone has strong objections to hybrid B+pointer, ping me here. :thumbsup:
